In fact you can run full flight simulators with high resolution on a phone today. For example xplane.

So I agree with your question. It shouldnt take a high end computer.

In fact the whole expensive vr googles things is ridiculous. It does take a 1080p or higher display per eye . Maybe 4k per eyes if you have very good vision. But moderate computers and graphics cards can put out 4k to two monitors today of any size whether they are on your desk or over your eyes.

Most vr headset are not higher resolutions than todays computer screens.

And almost any addon grahic card today will easily run two monitors at highest resolution. Right? Some will run three or four .onitors at highest resolution.

So im not sure why two monitors closer to your eyes using a lens would have a higher requirement.

As you mention you have to render the scene twice, once for each eye, but also the necessary frame rates for smooth movement are higher than for a regular 3d game, if you get framerate stutter it can lead to sickness.

you need quite a few things for a VR experience to feel right, and they are very very hard to do well. You need to render for each eye seperatealy, you need to over render the view usually to help keep view movement latency as low as possible. And total latency on the system needs to be incredibly low. Combine those demands on top of a modern game that already demands a lot on it's own and yeah, your little smart phone ain't gonna give you the same experience.
